common_name: Karpick Red Maple (Narrow Upright Red Maple)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring or fall in moist, slightly acidic, fertile soil in full sun; Karpick's narrow, upright-oval crown makes it a good fit for street tree strips and other confined spaces where wider red maple cultivars like October Glory would not fit.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply and regularly through the first two to three seasons to establish a strong root system. Karpick is an older red maple cultivar selected for its narrow, upright-oval to columnar crown, considerably tighter than broad-spreading cultivars like October Glory or Red Sunset, making it a useful choice for street tree strips, narrow side yards, and other confined planting sites where a wide-spreading shade tree would not fit. It grows at a fast rate for a red maple, bears small red flowers on bare branches in late winter as an early sign of spring, and develops orange-red fall color, though its color can be somewhat less uniformly brilliant from year to year than top-tier fall-color selections. Like other red maples, it tolerates a range of soil moisture, including occasional wet conditions, but performs best with consistent moisture in slightly acidic soil. Prune only to remove dead, damaged, or crossing branches, ideally in late fall or winter dormancy to avoid excessive sap bleeding.

common_name: Redpointe Red Maple (Pyramidal Brilliant-Red-Fall-Color Red Maple)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring or fall in moist, slightly acidic, fertile soil in full sun; Redpointe was selected in part for stronger branch attachment angles than older red maple cultivars, reducing the risk of included bark and storm breakage as the tree matures.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through establishment to help the root system develop before the tree faces summer heat and dry spells on its own. Redpointe is a patented red maple selection prized for its uniform, dense, pyramidal-oval crown and consistently brilliant, longer-lasting red fall color, along with notably stronger branch attachment angles than many older red maple cultivars, which reduces the risk of included bark and limb failure as the tree matures. It grows at a moderate to fast rate and bears the small red flowers typical of red maple on bare branches in late winter. It tolerates a range of soil conditions, including occasional wet sites and urban stress, and its tidy, predictable form has made it a popular choice for streets, lawns, and parking lot islands. Prune only to remove dead, damaged, or crossing branches, ideally in late fall or winter to minimize sap bleeding.
